    🙏 Ogoron¶

    "The titanic orc will avenge us all."

    Ogoron — meaning "titanic orc" in the demonic orchish tongue — is the faith of the orc peoples worldwide, centered in Augamouth on West Erisdar and in Yakut on Yak Island (where the Yak — smaller, modest orcs — carry the faith eastward). It teaches that a titanic orc savior will come to avenge orc-kind for every injustice, end the great war, and bring peace to all species.

    Ogoron is not a sect of Kirivs-bin. It is the orcs' own answer to demon honor — vengeance transformed into universal peace.

    Origins¶

    Ogoron emerged from Augamouth's long experience as a stigmatized martial kingdom on West Erisdar — feared, hired, and seldom heard. Orc oral tradition holds that during the worst persecution, a titanic orc — taller than a giant, scarred in every battle — appeared to a dying war-band and promised: what was taken will be returned, not as loot but as peace.

    No prophet is named because the promise is remembered as overheard, not delivered: the titan spoke to the wounded collectively, and they repeated it as they recovered.

    The faith crossed to the Demon Continent via Yak Island. When Yak orcs — a smaller, milder subrace of Orcs (the Yak people of Yakut, below Cubra Tribe and Estran, across the sea from Zakarutia) — established their own polity, they brought Ogoron with them intact, adding to it the Yak's characteristic modesty: the titan will come when orcs have proven they deserve peace, not before.

    Beliefs¶

    • A titanic orc will come — not metaphor. A literal, huge orc of legend — the avenger — will appear to settle the accounts of orc-kind: every pogrom, every mercenary betrayal, every child taken as labor. This is vengeance as jurisprudence: the ledger closed.
    • After the great war, all species will live in harmony — Ogoron is eschatologically universalist: the titan's war is the last war. Its aftermath is not orc supremacy but peace for all species, together. Orcs are avenged so that no one needs vengeance again.
    • Ogoron is inside all of their hearts — the titan is not merely a distant savior but a presence within every orc believer. To act with quiet, stubborn endurance is to let the titan breathe through you. Yak orcs in particular emphasize this inward presence over apocalyptic expectation.
    • Endurance is devotion — where Kirivs-bin venerates the duel and Tolumin venerates shared labor, Ogoron venerates carrying on: to hold the line, to raise children under stigma, to refuse to become what your persecutors claim you are.
    • No temples, but hearths — like the bin, Ogoron builds no temples; unlike the bin, it builds hearths — massive communal fire-pits in Augamouth longhouses and Yak stone circles where the tribe gathers to repeat the promise and add their own endurance to it.

    Practices¶

    • Hearth recitation — the promise recited antiphonally around the hearth at night: an elder speaks the wrongs remembered, the assembly answers "and the titan remembers too."
    • Scar-tending — Yak healers practice deliberate scar care after battles or accidents: cleaning, binding, and oiling scars to keep them legible. A scar is read as ledger entry — not shame but evidence.
    • Mercenary's pause — Augamouth orcs hired in foreign wars observe a day's pause before battle to ask whether this war is the war (it never is) and whether this employer deserves orc blood (sometimes not). Many contracts have been refused at this pause.
    • Yak modesty rite — Yak orcs on Yak Island add a small, daily practice: before any meal, a moment of silence with hands open, "to show we take only what peace would permit us."
    • Titan effigies — deliberately crude — Ogoron effigies of the titan are carved intentionally rough and left unfinished, "because we do not know his face until he comes."

    Relation to Kirivs-bin¶

    Separate — with mutual respect.

    • Ogoron is not Kirivs-bin and does not claim to be. It venerates a future titan, not Kirivis; its eschaton is universal peace after vengeance, not honor earned individually.
    • Nonetheless, orc and demon communities on the Demon Continent and Yak Island observe each other's rites without conflict. Mainland demons call Ogoron "the orcs' bin" and orcs call Kirivs-bin "the demons' hearth" — both inaccurate, both affectionate.
    • Yak Island is the continent's laboratory for coexistence: diablo Demonism, High Catmen Kludosy, Yak Ogoron, and demon plain Kirivs-bin share the same mountain roads and night markets. No faith there has attempted to absorb another.
    • Small syncretic minorities exist — orcs who honor both the titan and Kirivis, citing "the titan will need honorable lieutenants" — but neither orthodoxy recognizes dual belonging as doctrine; they tolerate it as personal piety.

    Influence¶

    • Majority: Augamouth (West Erisdar) — orc kingdom; state-recognized, hearth-centered
    • Majority: Yakut (Yak Island, Demon Continent) — the Yak people (smaller orcs, modest temperament); their Ogoron is quieter and more inward than Augamouth's martial variant
    • Diaspora: orc enclaves worldwide — wherever orcs labor as mercenaries, miners, or builders, a hearth-promise is repeated
    • Notable ally: Zakarutia has occasionally mediated between Augamouth and its neighbors; Zakarutian snake-matritarchs find Ogoron "legible" because vengeance-into-peace mirrors their own dynastic memory of betrayal and reunion
